Full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) values were linked within each doublet, and peak positions for the 3d₃/₂ components were fixed relative to their 3d₅/₂ counterparts to maintain physical consistency. The relative peak areas revealed that MoO₃ was the predominant species (89.5%), with minor contributions from Mo⁵⁺ (10.1%) and trace MoO₂ (0.4%), indicating a largely oxidized surface with partial reduction, likely due to oxygen vacancies or interfacial redox processes. The elevated chi-squared value suggested some residual misfit, potentially arising from unaccounted surface heterogeneity or subtle peak asymmetries, though the overall model provided a chemically reasonable interpretation of the sample’s oxidation state distribution.
